contract.review_scope: Body-level static contract; transitive application and called-module completeness are separate.
contract.purpose: Attach one shipment to a wave and assign caller-supplied pending statuses.
inputs_defaults: shipNum numeric(9), toWaveNum numeric(9), pendingSts numeric(3), processStamp nvarchar(100), userStamp nvarchar(30); required, no defaults.
null_and_invalid_input_behavior: NULL/missing shipment ID matches no rows. No positive/existing destination-wave validation. NULL pending status can violate nonnullable header status columns; unknown detail comparisons preserve the existing detail status.
output_shape: No intentional result set. No affected-row count is promised as an application result.

ordered_branches.explanation: Update the shipment header wave ID, both statuses to pendingSts, warehouse-local status dates and supplied/UTC stamps; return -1 on the immediately tested error.

Update its detail rows to the destination wave and set PREVIOUS_WAVE_NUM to that same destination. Raise STATUS1 to pendingSts only where its existing value is lower; otherwise retain STATUS1. Stamp and test the second statement error.

contract.status_and_quantity_effects: Header statuses are assigned unconditionally and can move downward; detail first status is only raised by its comparison. Quantities-at-status are not redistributed.
configuration_scope_and_precedence: No configuration lookup in this body; identifiers and status values are supplied by the caller.
error_and_return_handling: Each UPDATE is followed by @@ERROR check returning -1; there is no body-owned atomic transaction, rollback or rowcount validation. Header success can precede detail failure.
contract.transaction_ownership: No explicit transaction, commit, rollback, savepoint, TRY/CATCH or XACT_ABORT is introduced by this body; caller/session semantics remain authoritative.
concurrency: No body-owned snapshot or lock-based read/modify/write protocol; caller/session isolation governs concurrent observations.
contract.trigger_behavior: No INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE trigger on these target tables is present in the captured six-trigger inventory, except SHIPPING_CONTAINER has an INSERT-only trigger and WORK_INSTRUCTION has an INSERT-only trigger; updates/deletes here do not directly activate those INSERT events. Constraints and caller actions still apply.
external_handoffs_and_gaps: Application binding, effective permissions, permitted transitions and operational outcomes are not established.

NO_CAPTURED_REFERENCE means none of the credited channels in this exact retained corpus identified the table. It does not establish that the table is unused, obsolete, a backup, safe to delete, or absent from external application SQL.
Dynamic SQL, runtime-selected identifiers, external callers, client-generated SQL, uncaptured jobs and historical/other database code can use tables without a resolvable reference here.

The bounded lexer recognizes named SQL relation/DML positions and local aliases/CTEs; it is not the SQL Server binder. Unqualified names assume a unique captured name, not verified caller/default-schema resolution. Unsupported or ambiguous syntax remains explicit.

Identifier tokens and string-contained names are separate non-credit observations. Column names and configuration text can match table names; neither proves an executed table access.
Foreign keys are structural relationships and never count as procedure/function usage. View paths are catalog/source paths; attached trigger paths are possibilities, not proof the event fired.
